ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a DC power supply Us, with switching element VT connected in series above; the node after VT is connected to inductor L, and then connected to the load resistor R on the right, with load current id downward; this node is also connected to the bottom loop through the freewheeling diode VDR, and the positive and negative polarity of the output/load voltage ud is marked. Therefore, this circuit is a PWM-controlled buck chopper circuit. Reasoning: The average load voltage Ud of an ideal buck chopper is equal to the duty cycle D multiplied by the supply voltage Us. Given ton = 0.2 ms and toff = 0.4 ms, the period T = ton + toff = 0.6 ms. The duty cycle D = ton / T = 0.2 / 0.6 = 1/3. Thus Ud = D * Us = (1/3) * 300 V = 100 V.

method.method_draft: Identify the shown circuit as an ideal step-down chopper/buck converter with VT as the PWM switch. From the text take Us = 300 V, ton = 0.2 ms, toff = 0.4 ms. Compute the switching period T = ton + toff = 0.6 ms, hence duty ratio D = 0.2/0.6 = 1/3. Apply Ud = D Us to get Ud = 300 * 1/3 = 100 V.
